samples.visibleText: 1 2 3 4 5 1 / The question How do you check a line of code? Ada Mensah works with embedded firmware: code that controls a physical device. For Mosslink, an environmental sensor, she wrote the firmware, scheduled power states and built the bring-up fixture. Bring-up means checking a new board’s basic operation. Follow the connection from a firmware decision to something observable on the bench. Fictional prototype · Illustrative apparatus throughout. This is not an actual Mosslink device, circuit or measurement.

This is not an actual Mosslink device, circuit or measurement. 2 / The cycle Give the activities an order. Sleep → Measure → Transmit → repeat. This teaching loop shows how different activities can be organized across a repeated cycle. Scheduling gives a bench check an order of behavior to inspect.

Measured sleep and transmit current, combined with an assumed reporting interval, support a two-year projection. Separately, the longest continuous bench run was 72 hours observed. The two paths stay separate: 72 hours does not validate two years of endurance. Neither establishes field conditions or customer deployment. No exact currents, interval, capacity, original trace or run notebook is supplied. State tables, timing diagrams, current traces and bench checklists are working documents. The instrument labels here explain the evidence; they are not recovered records.

headings.text: A code decision. A check you can observe.

samples.visibleText: 1 2 3 4 5 5 / The answer, bounded A code decision. A check you can observe. Ada’s firmware and scheduling work connects to a physical check through the fixture she built. That is the contribution this apparatus explains—with the projection and observed run kept within their limits. Forty engineering samples were assembled; six were bench-tested; none went to customers. One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification is unfinished. This supports a bounded account of firmware and bring-up work, not whole-product ownership, field endurance or certification. Ada and Mosslink are fictional evaluation subjects.
